answer: Quadratic staking forces each Sybil node to lock collateral scaling with the square of its stake, yielding O(n^2) marginal cost. A 150% slashing penalty on equivocation creates a ledge where expected loss exceeds fork's net present value. Colluding clusters are confined to an island of liquidity-sink bonds that must be posted upfront, raising break-even capital. An orchard of tiered stakes diversifies risk so coordinated attacks need aggregate capital three times the block reward pool.
